title: Strathallan Park surplus declaration for school expansion
subtitle: Also: Francis Lane sale, Belwood child-care study, Fergus bypass option rejected, community grants, codes of conduct advocacy.
overview: Council declared Strathallan Park and two pedestrian walkways at 220 Strathallan Street, Fergus, surplus so the land can be conveyed to the Wellington Catholic District School Board for an expanded St. Joseph Catholic School and possibly a future high school {{vote:m7}}. The sale would still need Ministry of Education approval and a zoning amendment, which brings a public planning process. Councillors raised concerns about lost green space and traffic.

Council also approved the sale of Francis Lane in Elora to the abutting owner for a pedestrian walkway {{vote:m3}}. It directed staff to study a child-care and recreation facility in Belwood, with a report due June 24 {{vote:m11}}. It resolved that the second Fergus bypass option in the 2019 Transportation Master Plan is no longer viable {{vote:m12}}. It approved 2024 Community Impact Grant allocations {{vote:m5}} and supported AMO's call for stronger municipal codes of conduct {{vote:m13}}.

The Integrity Commissioner also delivered conflict of interest training, and the County Councillor for Ward 4 gave a County update. The meeting ran past its scheduled hours and curfew was extended twice.

decisions.detail: Council declared Strathallan Park and two walkways at 220 Strathallan Street surplus for conveyance to the Wellington Catholic District School Board, and authorized the CAO to sign the agreements.
Council approved closing and selling Francis Lane to the abutting landowner for a pedestrian walkway for $160,000, after 10 business days of public notice.
Council directed staff to investigate a child-care and recreation facility in Belwood with other governments and community partners, and to report back June 24 including letters of intent.
Council resolved that the 2019 Transportation Master Plan bypass option with a new bridge at County Road 29 is no longer viable, and to circulate this to Wellington County.
Council approved the grant allocations recommended by the Healthy Communities Advisory Committee and asked the working group to review the policy before the 2025 grant release.
Council endorsed AMO's call for provincial legislation to strengthen codes of conduct and enforcement, and to circulate the motion to federal and provincial officials.
Council authorized staff to gather Council and staff feedback on the 2023 to 2026 Strategic Plan before the 2025 budget process.
Council approved demolition of a garage at 203 Geddes Street and a front addition at 265 St. David Street South, and a Grand River Conservation Authority source protection funding agreement.

debate: On Strathallan Park, one councillor worried that residents in the ward would face over a kilometre to the nearest green space, and raised property values and traffic at Strathallan Street and Highway 6. Another noted that school-hours-only access would not serve stay-at-home parents and seniors.

Staff and the municipal solicitor said the sale needs Ministry approval and a zoning amendment. Council would see concept plans and traffic studies in that public process. Supporters cited the need for a local Catholic high school, since students are now bused to Guelph.

On the Belwood child-care motion, councillors supported child care but asked about staff capacity given the full business plan. They also wanted written commitments from partners before work began, and a lighter scope. The mayor said partner interest was strong and the timing tied to a developer's construction schedule.
The motion was amended to remove construction logistics, make site identification high level, name the Belwood Community Development Committee, and require letters of intent in the report.

On the Fergus bypass, the mover cited the ecological and heritage value of the Pierpoint Fly Fishing Nature Reserve, the fly-fishing tourism value, and that the bridge would land in a residential area. Other councillors supported the motion.
